claim: A walking body clears a rise of footOffset - floordist, where MoveDude passes floordist = (bottom - z)/4: about three quarters of the half body, roughly 6,400 z for a 16,960 standing human (6,548 to 6,659 measured as the walk frames change the body's height). It is not a fixed autostep, and a step down is never refused: nothing stops a body walking off a ledge, the line is drawn at the landing.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/actor.cpp:4450-4470 (MoveDude: bz = (bottom-z)/4 passed to ClipMove as the floor distance)

NBlood/source/build/src/clip.cpp:876-888 (cliptestsector, default case: blocks entry when the next floor is over 256 higher and posz >= daz2-(flordist-1); nothing tests a drop), taken because NBlood/source/blood/src/blood.cpp:1890 (app_main) sets enginecompatibilitymode to ENGINE_19960925, which has no case of its own

Measured by the headless bot on AGTST18, 2026-08-27, not rerun (radius 192, height 17,316, flordist 2,220, foot offset ~8,880: 6,659); bloodmap's player profile uses max_step 4,096 as a deliberately conservative at-rest threshold.
use: Treat rises up to ~4,096 as steps everyone takes and up to ~6,400 as the engine's own limit; anything taller is a jump or a wall.

checked.how: actor.cpp MoveDude (4435): 4450 bz = (bottom-pSprite->z)/4, 4470 ClipMove(..., wd, tz, bz, CLIPMASK0). blood.cpp:1890 (app_main) sets enginecompatibilitymode = ENGINE_19960925, which no case of cliptestsector names, so the default case (clip.cpp:876-888) runs: 'if (daz2 < daz-(1<<8) && (sec2->floorstat&1) == 0) if (posz >= daz2-(flordist-1)) return 1' at 880-881; no test on a drop. 8,880 - 2,220 = 6,660. The AGTST18 bot figures are a dated run, not repeated.
